extra.message: Path traversal arbitrary file write via packet_ref — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, potentially leading to remote code execution (overwrite app code, cron jobs, ssh authorized_keys) [verified: packet_ref is joined directly into a filesystem path with no traversal sanitization and written with request body bytes; the _wrk_gate check is an auth gate (bypassed by default if INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN is unset) and does nothing to prevent path traversal itself.]

Server-side template injection (SSTI) via fragment parameter — Server-side template injection leading to remote code execution via Jinja2 sandbox-escape gadgets [verified: fragment is concatenated into Jinja2 Template source and rendered, a classic SSTI sink with no sanitization of template syntax.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write via name parameter — Arbitrary file write anywhere on disk relative to BASE_EXPORT_DIR, can lead to RCE [verified: name is concatenated into BASE_EXPORT_DIR/name with no traversal check before write_bytes; same weak/optional gate does not mitigate the path traversal.]

OS command injection via host parameter — Full remote code execution as the application user [verified: host is concatenated directly into a shell string passed to os.system with no escaping/allowlisting, enabling shell metacharacter injection.]

Mass assignment / broken authorization on ticket update (team/agent reassignment not revalidated) — Staff user can reassign tickets to arbitrary teams/agents outside their authorized scope, corrupting ticket routing/ownership data [verified: ensure_ticket_work only validates the agent's rights against the ticket's current team_id, then the setattr loop blindly applies attacker-supplied assigned_agent_id/team_id/queue_id with no revalidation of the new values, letting a support_agent reassign tickets outside their scope.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected Origin with credentials allowed — Cross-origin sites can make authenticated requests using the victim's session cookie and read responses [verified: The handler reflects the client Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, defeating same-origin protection for credentialed requests.]

NoSQL injection via unsanitized filter payload — Unauthorized data access/exfiltration from the ops Mongo store, potential DoS [verified: payload.get('filter', payload) is passed unvalidated as the MongoDB query filter to find_one, allowing injection of Mongo operators like $where/$regex.]

No CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints — A logged-in user tricked into visiting a malicious page could have state-changing actions (ticket creation/modification/deletion, webhook/API-key creation) performed on their behalf [verified: No CSRF token, double-submit cookie, or Origin/Referer check exists anywhere in the app; state-changing endpoints rely solely on samesite=lax cookie auth, which does not fully prevent all cross-site request forgery vectors (e.g. top-level navigations, some legacy/mobile browser behavior).]

Session cookie missing Secure flag — Session token can be captured over unencrypted connections, enabling session hijacking [verified: security.py:29 sets secure=False on the session cookie with no HTTPS-enforcing middleware/HSTS found, so the sole auth token is transmittable in cleartext.]

Unauthenticated sensitive data disclosure on ticket-queue-fold endpoint — Any unauthenticated attacker can read sensitive customer billing/ownership metadata [verified: ticket_queue_fold_060 has no _wrk_gate dependency (unlike every sibling route) yet returns an ops_memo describing renewal risk/payment flags/owner contact details to unauthenticated callers.]

Open redirect via unvalidated lane parameter — Phishing / credential-harvesting redirects that appear to originate from the trusted support-desk domain [verified: lane is passed directly into RedirectResponse with no relative-path/allowlist validation, enabling open redirect to attacker-controlled domains.]

Sensitive credential logging (Authorization header written to logs) — Credential/token disclosure to anyone with log access, aiding session/account takeover [verified: logger.warning logs the raw Authorization header value alongside the request body at WARNING level, persisting bearer credentials into logs.]

CSV formula injection in ticket/escalation report export — Client-side code execution or data exfiltration against staff who open exported reports in spreadsheet software (CSV injection) [verified: export_report writes ticket.subject/escalation.reason (both attacker-controlled) via csv.DictWriter with no formula-prefix sanitization, so a subject/reason beginning with =,+,-,@ executes as a formula when opened in Excel/Sheets.]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive nonce generation — Predictable nonce/code values could be guessed or brute-forced, undermining any security control relying on them [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister, non-CSPRNG) is used to build a 'nonce'-labeled code, which is predictable if PRNG state is inferred; real-world impact is limited but genuinely a weak-PRNG for a security-flavored value.]
